clue.text: Gradually includes Times in back copies of favourites

indicators.note: includes means the multiplication word is held inside the reversed pair
back tells us the two copies of the pets are read in reverse

parts.note: favourites are PETS; two copies of the word give PETSPETS
BY is the multiplication word, as in three by four

explanation.surface: A library-style scene: back issues of a favourite newspaper, The Times, being collected over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it is the multiplication word, as in 3 by 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something one stage at a time is doing it gradually, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Film announced some century breaks

indicators.note: breaks means the century letter splits the spoken word
announced means spoken, so we use a word that sounds like some

parts.note: some is heard here as sum
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a century

explanation.surface: A cricket commentator mentioning a few centuries scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Scum is a film of dirt or froth floating on the surface of a liquid.

clue.text: Mixer is briefly, perhaps, wide open

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: in cricket a wide is one kind of extra run, hence 'perhaps'
overt means open, not hidden

explanation.surface: A cocktail mixer described as wide open.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a bad delivery that gives the batting side an extra run.
explanation.definitionFit: A good mixer at parties is a sociable, outgoing person, which is what an extrovert is.

clue.text: Hold up electronic lighter

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to grab is to seize or hold
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: Holding up a battery-powered cigarette lighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lighter' looks like the smoker's gadget; a lighter is a flat-bottomed boat for unloading ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed cargo boat, essentially a barge.

clue.text: Leak note to skip part of book?

definitions.text: note to skip part of book?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: a footnote telling you to jump to another page

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into SEE PAGE and it is the cross-reference a book prints.
explanation.definitionFit: Seepage is the slow escape of liquid through a gap, exactly a leak.

clue.text: Beg for goods ditched by man and chief

indicators.note: ditched by means the good letters are thrown out of both words

parts.note: gent is short for gentleman, a man
great means chief or principal
G is the abbreviation for good; goods are two Gs

explanation.surface: Pleading for merchandise that a man and his boss threw away.
explanation.walkthrough: One G comes out of GENT and one out of GREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to plead earnestly, a formal synonym for begging.

clue.text: Tense time with old academics?

parts.note: the AUT, the Association of University Teachers, was a former UK lecturers' union

explanation.surface: A nervous moment among elderly dons, perhaps at an anxious meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The AUT merged into the University and College Union in 2006, hence 'old'.
explanation.definitionFit: Taut and tense both describe something stretched tight or a nervous state.

clue.text: Cut top off beam later on

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: a rafter is a roof beam

explanation.surface: Trimming the end of a roof beam at a later stage.
explanation.definitionFit: After means following in time, so it can stand for the adverb later on.

clue.text: Thinner internet up for development

indicators.note: development means the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A slimmer internet set up for development work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thinner' looks like a comparative adjective; it is the solvent noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Turpentine is a solvent used to dilute oil paints, a paint thinner.

clue.text: Change of old term for Andromeda Nebula, for one?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an old British coin, small change in the past

definitions.text: term for Andromeda Nebula, for one?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words

explanation.walkthrough: A farthing was a quarter of an old penny; split it as FAR THING for the distant galaxy.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a pre-decimal coin worth a quarter penny, and splits into a description of a remote object.

clue.text: Grumble without Mike, say

indicators.note: without tells us the letter for Mike is dropped from the grumble word

parts.note: to mutter is to grumble under one's breath
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone complaining without a microphone, so nobody hears what they say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example', but it is the verb definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter something is to speak or voice it, a direct synonym for say.

clue.text: Fan found in abandoned farm vehicle

parts.note: EX means former, something abandoned or left behind
a tractor is a farm vehicle

explanation.surface: An enthusiast discovered hiding inside a derelict tractor.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor fan draws stale air out of a kitchen or bathroom, so the device is a fan.

clue.text: Oscar intercepts letter with a counterfeit permit

indicators.note: intercepts means the Oscar letter cuts into the middle of the reworked letters
counterfeit means fake, so the letters of letter and a are reworked

parts.note: Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone tampering with mail and faking a document to get a licence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'counterfeit' shuffles LETTER A into TLERATE, and 'intercepts' puts O after the first T.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate something is to allow it to happen, so it can stand for the verb permit.

clue.text: Sweet betrothal partly rejected

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters are read in reverse
partly means only part of the word betrothal is used

explanation.surface: A sweet engagement that was partly called off.
explanation.walkthrough: Read betrothal backwards (LAHTORTEB) and the five letters sit inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake, a kind of dessert or sweet course.

clue.text: For whom coping could be part of the job

definitions.text: For whom coping could be part of the job

parts.words: For whom coping could be part of the job
parts.note: coping looks like managing stress, but it is the top course of stones on a wall, built by a skilled tradesman

explanation.walkthrough: Coping is the capping layer of masonry along the top of a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who cuts and lays stone builds walls, including their coping stones.

clue.text: Globe, maybe, within which one may operate

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a playhouse, the Globe in London being an example
second meaning: an operating room in a hospital

explanation.walkthrough: The Globe is Shakespeare's playhouse in London; a surgeon works in an operating one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a playhouse for drama and a hospital room for surgery.

clue.text: The Cloth meant to give dry services?

definitions.text: The Cloth meant to give dry services?

parts.words: The Cloth meant to give dry services?
parts.note: the Cloth suggests the clergy giving dull church services, but it is a fabric for drying the tea service

explanation.walkthrough: 'The Cloth' is a common term for the clergy; here services are cups and saucers.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen towel is used for drying crockery such as cups and saucers after washing up.

clue.text: Missile shelter offering protection for free

indicators.note: the shelter offers protection by wrapping around the word for free

parts.note: a tent is a simple shelter
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: A missile bunker giving people cover at no cost.
explanation.definitionFit: Trident is the submarine-launched nuclear weapon system carried by the Royal Navy.

clue.text: Ultra vires unopened text message primarily scrapped

indicators.note: scrapped means broken up, so the collected letters are rearranged
unopened means the first letter of vires is taken off
primarily means only the first letter of message is used

explanation.surface: A legal note that a text message beyond someone's powers was mostly deleted.
explanation.walkthrough: Ultra vires is Latin for beyond one's powers; 'scrapped' shuffles IRES, TEXT and M.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding radical views, the same as a fanatic.

clue.text: Compound doubling metal price

indicators.note: doubling back means folding back, so the metal word is read in reverse

parts.note: tin is a metal
a rate is a price or charge

explanation.surface: The price of some metal has doubled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubling' looks like twice as much, but it means turning back on itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A nitrate is a chemical compound, a salt of nitric acid.

clue.text: Learns about shielding knight put in difficulty

indicators.note: shielding means the rearranged letters surround the knight letter
about means the letters of learns are moved around

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A student learning about a knight's shield and running into trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensnarl is to tangle or trap, leaving someone stuck in trouble.

clue.text: Secure satellite broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken over the air, so we want a word that sounds like the moon

parts.note: Titan is a satellite, the largest moon of Saturn

explanation.surface: Arranging a satellite broadcast that is safely locked in.
explanation.definitionFit: To tighten a fastening is to make it firm, so it can stand for the verb secure.

clue.text: Swing section up on drugs by the sound of it

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a part is a section

indicators.note: this means spoken, so the drug letters are heard aloud

parts.note: E is slang for ecstasy, so drugs are Es

explanation.surface: Part of a swing band playing while high.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal bar hung from ropes, a swing used by acrobats.

clue.text: Too much crammed into flash phrase

indicators.note: crammed into means the over-the-top abbreviation is packed inside the flash word

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a flash
OTT, over the top, means too much

explanation.surface: An excessive amount squeezed into a showy turn of phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short saying adopted as a guiding principle, a type of phrase.

clue.text: Tribute perfectly covering saint

indicators.note: covering means the phrase wraps around the saint letter

parts.note: to a T means perfectly

explanation.surface: A tribute that perfectly covers a saint's life.
explanation.definitionFit: A toast is a tribute paid by raising glasses and drinking to someone.

clue.text: Launch reportedly smashing sci-fi franchise

parts.note: to launch something is to start it

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard, so the two words are spoken together

parts.note: a smashing is a wreck, said aloud here

explanation.surface: A rocket launch said to have been a smash for a space franchise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smashing' looks like praise, but it is a wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Star Trek is the long-running space-opera series of television shows and films.

clue.text: Dead poet identified by bones raised below bottom of crypt

indicators.note: in a down clue the bones sit below the crypt letter
bottom means the last letter of crypt
in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards

parts.note: ossa is the Latin plural of os, bone

explanation.surface: A dead poet identified from skeletal remains lifted out of a crypt.
explanation.walkthrough: Torquato Tasso was a 16th-century Italian poet, author of Jerusalem Delivered.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasso was an Italian Renaissance poet who died in 1595.

clue.text: Problem for viewer surfaces at injury time in finals

indicators.note: finals means the last letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A footballer's eye problem surfaces during injury time in cup finals.
explanation.definitionFit: A stye is an inflamed swelling on the eyelid, an ailment of the eye.

clue.text: Colleague in same company perhaps ignoring British deadlock

indicators.note: ignoring means the British abbreviation is left out of the colleague word

parts.note: a stablemate is a colleague from the same company or stable

explanation.surface: A workplace standoff where a co-worker refuses to deal with the British side.
explanation.definitionFit: Stalemate in chess is a position where no move is possible, hence any impasse.

clue.text: Spell "just in time" using only some of the letters

indicators.text: using only some of the letters
indicators.note: the clue tells us to use only part of the quoted phrase's letters, running across its words

explanation.surface: A spelling instruction about writing the phrase "just in time".
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like the instruction to write letters out; it is the definition, a period of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A stint is a period spent doing a job, just as a spell of work is.

clue.text: Clear web sites centrally

parts.note: a net is a web or mesh

indicators.note: centrally means we take the middle letter of sites

explanation.surface: Tidying up websites from the middle out.
explanation.definitionFit: Nett means after deductions, so to clear a sum as profit is to nett it.

clue.text: Navy possibly daring to be PC

parts.note: navy is a shade of blue
bottle is British slang for nerve or daring

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the navy dares to be politically correct.
explanation.walkthrough: PC here is a police constable; bluebottle is old British slang for a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Bluebottle is dated slang for a uniformed policeman, after the blue uniform.
